title: Your First Query
description: Write your first useQuery hook, handle loading and error states, and understand query keys.

data.text: **useQuery** is the primary hook for fetching data in React Query. It accepts a configuration object with a unique queryKey and an async queryFn, and returns an object containing the data, loading state, error state, and several utility flags â€” all managed automatically.
In React Query v5, useQuery takes a single options object with queryKey and queryFn as the only required fields. This is a change from earlier versions where the hook accepted positional arguments.

data.text: The old syntax useQuery(queryKey, queryFn) is no longer valid in v5. Always use useQuery({ queryKey, queryFn }) â€” this is a common migration pitfall.

data.text: Query keys are how React Query identifies and organizes cached data. They are simple arrays of values. Every value that changes the response should be included in the key â€” typically resource type plus identifying parameters.

data.title: Query Key Patterns
items: ['users', userId] â€” one specific user by ID
['posts', postId, 'comments'] â€” comments for a specific post
['todos', 'filtered', filter, status] â€” filtered todos with multiple params
['search', queryString, page] â€” search results with pagination

terms.definition: A unique array that identifies a query in the React Query cache. Must include all variables that affect the response. Used for caching, deduplication, and invalidation.
An async function that returns a Promise resolving to the query data. Called by React Query when the cache is empty or stale.
A boolean flag that is true only on the first render when no cached data exists. Distinct from isFetching, which is true during background refetches too.
A boolean flag set to true when the query function throws an error. Paired with the error property containing the Error object.

data.text: Real queries almost always depend on variables â€” a user ID, a search term, a page number. Include all variables in the queryKey. React Query automatically creates separate cache entries for each unique key combination.

data.text: The enabled option controls whether the query runs automatically. Set it to false when you want to fetch data only after a certain condition is met â€” such as when a userId becomes available. This is the foundation for dependent queries, covered in the next lesson.

data.title: Build a User Directory
data.description: Create a UserDirectory component that fetches and displays a list of users from a mock API. Practice writing a clean useQuery component with proper loading, error, and empty states.
steps: Create a mock API function fetchUsers that returns a Promise<User[]> after a 500ms delay using setTimeout
Write the UserDirectory component using useQuery with queryKey ['users'] and queryFn fetchUsers
Show a loading spinner or text while isLoading is true
Show a styled error message if isError is true
Show a friendly message when data is an empty array
Render each user as a card with name and email
Add a second component UserProfile that fetches a single user by ID with queryKey ['user', userId]
data.expectedOutcome: A fully working user directory with smooth loading, error, and empty states. The UserProfile component correctly uses a parameterized query key and the enabled option.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useQuery requires queryKey and queryFn in an options object (v5 syntax)
Returns data, isLoading, isError, error, isFetching, and more
queryKey must be unique and include all variables that affect the response
queryFn must return a Promise â€” use async/await for clarity
enabled controls whether the query runs automatically
isLoading is true only on the first render with no cache data
isFetching is true on every fetch, including background refetches
data.takeaway: useQuery is the fundamental hook of React Query. Mastering its return values and options is the foundation for everything else in this course.
